regions.label: Office-style ribbon: FILE button, HOME/EDIT/ACCOUNT tabs, username with avatar, HOME panel with command groups Table, Export, Page, Feedback
Gray start page: title 'Dbdesigner.id' and tagline, then two columns of link lists (Recent, Help, New Feature, News)

evidence.note: Fixed ribbon frame along the top: tabs, user identity at top right, content area below
Ribbon tabs. The active HOME tab is shown in blue with a raised border. Clicking EDIT on the live page switches the ribbon panel (EDIT's panel is empty).

patterns.rationale: Seen only on the live page: clicking FILE slides in a left backstage panel (New/Open/Properties/Account/Logout, plus an Open list with search) over a dimming scrim. The capture shows only the FILE trigger.

evidence.note: Blue FILE button that opens the backstage drawer
The start-page sections are plain heading and link lists, not bounded cards

structure.layout: desktop web app: Office-style ribbon across the top over a gray start page with a title block and a two-column grid of link lists

aesthetics.typography: 'Chinese Quote' (falls back to a system sans) for the ribbon, section labels and links. Segoe UI (rendered as Open Sans-like) for the h2 title and h3 tagline.
aesthetics.typeScale: Title 30px/400, tagline 24px/300, section labels 20px/400, links 14px, ribbon labels 11px and group captions 10px. Weight contrast is low; hierarchy comes from size alone.

notes: Copies the Microsoft Office 2013 ribbon closely: a blue FILE button that opens a backstage panel, tabs whose active one is outlined, and large icon-over-label command buttons in groups with gray captions underneath (Table, Export, Page, Feedback). The Page group holds compact rows (700 px, 1500 px, 100 %) plus grid and fit icons. Feedback has a red speech-bubble icon. The start page is like Office's Recent/Help start screen: blue link lists, typos such as 'Inroduction', 'repot' and 'theor', and three sunglasses emoji after the tagline. There are no rounded corners and no shadows. The ribbon itself has no codebook entry, so I proposed 'ribbon-toolbar'.
